title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: EARL'S LAKE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Earl, a retired mail carrier from Duluth, Minnesota.
Forty years of walking through snow. He lived five minutes from a giant lake. And he never learned to swim.
Then, at sixty seven, his granddaughter asked him one question. Grandpa, will you swim with me this summer?

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE QUESTION
segments.quote: You must do the thing you think you cannot do.
segments.author: Eleanor Roosevelt
lines: Earl said, maybe. Which, in grandpa language, means no.
That night he opened a library book by Eleanor Roosevelt, the former first lady, and found this:
You must do the thing you think you cannot do.
The next morning, Earl signed up for adult swim lessons at the community pool.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE SHALLOW END
segments.quote: I'm not afraid of storms, for I'm learning how to sail my ship.
segments.author: Louisa May Alcott
lines: First lesson. The water came up to his belly button. He panicked anyway.
His teacher, Keisha, was twenty two. She told him a line from Little Women, by Louisa May Alcott:
I'm not afraid of storms, for I'm learning how to sail my ship.
Earl didn't have to be brave yet. He just had to be learning. So he came back Thursday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE SAME MISTAKE
segments.quote: Failure is not fatal but failure to change might be.
segments.author: John Wooden
lines: Every week, Earl held his breath and sank. Like a sack of mail.
Keisha pointed to a poster in the locker room, from the famous basketball coach John Wooden:
Failure is not fatal but failure to change might be.
So Earl changed one thing. He breathed out slowly. Little bubbles. And for the first time, he floated.
Now, I float very well. But I'm built for it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: ONE LAP
segments.quote: No great thing is created suddenly, any more than a bunch of grapes or a fig.
segments.author: Epictetus
lines: Weeks passed. One lap took him four minutes. A teenager passed him twice. Doing the backstroke.
Earl wanted to quit. His neighbor Hank, who reads old Greek thinkers, told him what Epictetus said:
No great thing is created suddenly, any more than a bunch of grapes or a fig.
So Earl stopped timing himself. He just kept showing up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE NEW GUY
segments.quote: Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: In January, a new man joined the class. Ray, seventy one, gripping the wall like it owed him money.
Earl thought, not my problem. Then he remembered a card on his fridge, from the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius:
Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
So Earl got in next to Ray and said, breathe out. Little bubbles. Trust me.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE LAKE
segments.quote: A life is not important except for the impact it has on other lives.
segments.author: Jackie Robinson
lines: June. The lake was cold. Very cold. Earl swam out to the buoy with his granddaughter, and back.
On the beach, Ray was teaching his own grandson to blow bubbles.
Earl thought of a line from Jackie Robinson's life story:
A life is not important except for the impact it has on other lives.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Do the hard thing. Keep learning. Change. Be patient. Be good. Lift others.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Do the thing you think you can't. Keep learning. Change what isn't working. Be patient. Be the good guy. And lift someone else up.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And bring a towel. That lake is cold.
